notes: v2.136 (2026-11-25, evening run): 135th tower 'Sled' (a red pull-rope diagonal over a long yellow deck on a green runner rail with blue runner feet — a sled silhouette to demolish, 33 blocks, 6 clusters sizes 14/9/4/2/2/2, all 4 colours, no singletons, 0 canonical duplicates). Completes the pair with the Sled co-play prompt already in COPLAY (from the earlier bulk prompt batch: put a soft toy on a blanket, hold the corners, and pull it along the floor saying 'pull… glide… stop!', take turns pulling, and a grown-up can pull you on the blanket too; pretend sled only — a blanket or towel on a smooth floor indoors, no real snow, no hills, and a grown-up is always pulling). Sled research: pulling is heavy work — proprioceptive input that calms and organizes a toddler (OT guidance); sitting tall on a moving blanket-sled builds core strength and balance, and the child calling 'stop'/'go' is the control; pull-along play from ~15–18 months teaches cause and effect (pull the string, the toy follows) and the transporting schema. The indoor blanket form is already the prompt's form — no real sled or snow needed.
